title: Reclining on silk-lined couches, fruit hanging within reach.
subtitle: Rest and ease in the first two gardens
then: Ikrimah and Qatadah said istabraq is {reward}thick silk brocade{/reward}. Ibn Masud said: {idea}this is the lining, so what about the outside?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says the fruit comes down from the branches to whoever wants it, reclining or not.
now: You come home after a twelve-hour shift and fall onto the sofa. Even the remote is too far away. {reward}A rest where everything you want comes to you{/reward} is what this verse describes, after a life of effort.
old: Rest is something I have to earn every day, and it never lasts.
new: The effort of this life ends in a rest where everything is within reach.
try: When you rest tonight, say: O Allah, grant me the rest of the gardens.

title: Rest with fruit in reach. Which favor would you deny?
subtitle: The refrain after the couches and low fruit
then: After describing {reward}couches of brocade and fruit hanging low{/reward}, the refrain asks again. Ibn Kathir cites the verses where the fruit bunches hang low within reach. {idea}Ease is named as a favor in itself.{/idea}
now: You are tired in a way sleep does not fix: caring for a newborn, nursing a parent, two jobs. {idea}Tiredness spent in good is not wasted.{/idea} {reward}It is walking toward a rest that does not end.{/reward}
old: My exhaustion is just the price of life.
new: Tiredness in doing good is a road toward a rest I cannot deny.
try: Offer your tiredness today to Allah, and ask Him to accept it.

title: Companions whose eyes are only for their spouses.
subtitle: Faithfulness as a reward
then: Ibn Abbas and Qatadah said these are {reward}wives who restrain their glances, desiring none but their husbands{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says the verse is also proof that {idea}believing jinn will enter Paradise{/idea}.
now: You see couples who have been together forty years, still holding hands at the bus stop. What moves you is not beauty, it is that they still only see each other. {reward}The verse names faithfulness as a reward.{/reward}
old: Loyalty in love is rare and old-fashioned.
new: Faithfulness is so precious that Allah names it among the rewards of Paradise.
try: Do one small thing today to show loyalty to your spouse or family.

title: A love that looks nowhere else. Which favor would you deny?
subtitle: The refrain after the faithful companions
then: The refrain follows the description of companions {reward}who desire none but their spouses{/reward}. Ibn Kathir reports one will say: by Allah, I see nothing in Paradise more handsome or beloved to me than you, {idea}so praise be to Allah who made you for me{/idea}.
now: You worry about your marriage, or whether you will ever marry, or about a love that went wrong. {reward}A love free of fear is promised{/reward}, and its first words there are praise to Allah.
old: Love always comes with worry and pain.
new: A secure, faithful love is a favor Allah promises.
try: Make a dua today for the marriage of someone you know, or your own.

title: As if they were rubies and coral.
subtitle: Purity and radiance
then: Mujahid and Al-Hasan said they are {reward}as pure as rubies and white as marjan{/reward}, here meaning pearls. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith that the first group to enter Paradise will {idea}look like the moon on a full night{/idea}.
now: You see filters, before-and-after photos, the endless effort to look a certain way. Beauty here fades and needs maintaining. {reward}The beauty described there is like gemstones: it does not wear out.{/reward}
old: Beauty is something you have to chase and protect.
new: The beauty of Paradise is pure and lasting, a gift, not a chase.
try: Compliment someone today on a quality of character, not appearance.

title: Pure as rubies. Which favor would you deny?
subtitle: The refrain after rubies and coral
then: Ibn Kathir cites the hadith of Anas: {reward}a place in Paradise the size of a whip is better than the world and all on it{/reward}. After the image of rubies and coral, {idea}the refrain asks again{/idea}.
now: You spend months saving for a bigger flat, a nicer car. You measure your life in square meters. {reward}A strip of Paradise the length of a whip is worth more than all of it.{/reward}
old: A bigger place here would make me happy.
new: The smallest place in Paradise is worth more than the whole world.
try: Before you buy something big this week, ask yourself what it is worth next to Jannah.

title: Is the reward for good anything but good?
subtitle: Ihsan answered with ihsan
then: Ibn Kathir says only good is the fitting reward for those who do good, citing: {reward}for those who did good is the best, and more{/reward}. He adds these blessings {idea}cannot be earned merely by deeds, but by Allah's favor and bounty{/idea}.
now: You hold the door, you cover a colleague's shift, you call your mother when you would rather not. Nobody thanks you. {idea}The verse asks a question that already holds its answer.{/idea} {reward}Good comes back as good.{/reward}
old: Doing good just means people take advantage of me.
new: Good is never lost. Allah answers it with good, and more.
try: Do one act of ihsan today, a little more than what is required.

title: Good repaid with good. Which favor would you deny?
subtitle: The refrain after the reward of ihsan
then: Ibn Kathir says all these blessings are {reward}tremendous{/reward}, given by Allah's favor rather than earned by deeds alone. {idea}After all of these, He asks again{/idea}: which of the favors of your Lord would you deny?
now: You did something good last week and felt a small glow of pride. {idea}Even the chance to do it was His gift{/idea}, and so is His accepting it. {reward}Favor on top of favor.{/reward}
old: My good deeds are my own achievement.
new: That Allah lets me do good, and then rewards it, is a double favor.
try: After your next good deed, say Alhamdulillah for being allowed to do it.

title: And below those two, two more gardens.
subtitle: Paradise has levels

row.title: two more
sub: silver, for those on the right

then: Ibn Kathir says these gardens are {idea}lower in virtue and status{/idea} than the first two. Abu Musa said: {reward}two gardens of gold for the muqarrabin, two of silver for the people of the right{/reward}.
now: You think you will never be one of the very best: the night-prayer people, the ones who memorized it all. {reward}There is a garden for those on the right too.{/reward} {idea}And you can still aim higher.{/idea}
old: If I cannot be the best, there is no place for me.
new: Paradise has levels: room to be saved, and room to rise higher.
try: Pick one small extra deed to aim a level higher this week.

title: A garden for every level. Which favor would you deny?
subtitle: The refrain after the second pair of gardens

row.title: also for those on the right

then: Ibn Kathir says the first two gardens are for {idea}the near ones{/idea}, and these for {reward}the people of the right{/reward}. Even the lower rank is a pair of gardens, and the refrain asks again which favor would be denied.
now: You compare yourself to the most pious person you know and feel hopeless. {reward}Allah made room for people who are trying, not only for those who have arrived.{/reward}
old: I am not good enough for Paradise.
new: Allah prepared gardens for ordinary believers too. That is a favor.
try: Tell yourself one thing you do well for Allah, and ask Him to accept it.

title: Dark green, deep with water.
subtitle: Gardens so watered they look almost black
then: Ibn Abbas said mudhammatan means {reward}they have become dark green because of extensive watering{/reward}. Muhammad bin Kab said it means {idea}full of greenery{/idea}.
now: You fly over a desert and suddenly see a field of deep green where a river runs. Your eye goes straight to it. {reward}Green that deep means life.{/reward}
old: One shade of green is like another.
new: Even the color of the gardens speaks of endless life and water.
try: Find the greenest thing near you today and look at it for a minute with gratitude.

title: Deep green life. Which favor would you deny?
subtitle: The refrain after the dark green gardens
then: After the image of gardens {reward}dark green from abundant water{/reward}, the refrain returns. For the first listeners in a dry land, {idea}deep green was the picture of wealth and life{/idea}.
now: You watch your lawn or your potted plants turn brown in a heatwave, and you water them every evening anyway. {reward}There is a garden that never needs saving.{/reward}
new: The gardens Allah promises stay green forever.
try: Water a plant or a tree today and say: O Allah, make my place green in Jannah.

title: Two springs gushing in them.
subtitle: Water that wells up without end

picture.label: Two pairs, two kinds of springs

then: Ibn Abbas said naddakhatan means {reward}gushing{/reward}, and that free flowing is stronger than gushing, which is why the first gardens are higher. Ad-Dahhak said these springs are {idea}full of water and constantly gushing{/idea}.
now: You turn on a weak shower on a cold morning and wish for pressure. You see a fountain in a park and kids running through it. {reward}Even the lower gardens have springs that never stop.{/reward}
old: A lower rank in Paradise would hardly be worth it.
new: Even the lower gardens overflow. Every level is more than I deserve.
try: Thank Allah today for one ordinary thing, like hot water, by name.
